guidelines.detail: new guideline (The description states that the tool gives a list of materials, a list of tools and ordering choices, with no stated wait. The generated model instead modeled the receipt of the list as an intermediate catch event (X3), and the reference has three service tasks for these presentations (M9, M10, M11). The closest documented guidelines do not address this case, and the closest learned guideline LRN-)

same as LRN-087 (The description (S3) states the system gives lists of materials and tools plus ordering choices, with no waiting condition. The reference has a serviceTask 'List required materials' (M9), while the generated model has an intermediateCatchEvent for the same list (X3). That is a choice of element type, not a label issue. The label pairs (P2-P5) are close matches, and documented FID-03 already covers)

refines GW-04 (The description says the tool gives a list of materials, a list of tools, and ordering choices for each part, with no stated order and no decision among them. The reference models these three presentations as concurrent branches with a parallel split (M23) and a parallel join (M24). The generated model has neither gateway (both are missing), so it diverges structurally. GW-04 already covers parall)

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description says an online service or software system presents a list of items or a set of selectable options to the user as a step of the process, and it does not say that the process waits for an incoming message, signal, time or condition at that point: Model each such presentation as one bpmn:serviceTask performed by the system, placed in the sequence where the description places it, and labeled with the action verb and object the description states. Do not model it as an intermediate catch event or a start event that waits for a message, and do not add a separate receive element for it. Model each stated list or option set as its own service task, so that every presented list or option set has a counterpart.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description says an online service or software system presents a list of items or a set of selectable options to the user as a step of the process, and it does not say that the process waits for an incoming message, signal, time or condition at that point

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description lists several items that the system provides at the same time, with no stated order among them and no condition choosing between them, so all of them are delivered: Model each of these items as its own concurrent branch. Open the branches with a parallel split gateway and close them with a parallel join gateway before the shared continuation. Do not sequence the items one after another and do not place an exclusive or inclusive gateway among them.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description lists several items that the system provides at the same time, with no stated order among them and no condition choosing between them, so all of them are delivered

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states that the system or tool gives the user guidance or information on how to carry out an activity, and the user then performs that activity: Model the delivery of the guidance as its own task, labeled with the verb and object the description uses for that delivery, and model the performance of the activity as a separate later task (performed by the user). Do not merge the delivery and the performance into one task named after the performed work, and do not assign the performance to the system.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states that the system or tool gives the user guidance or information on how to carry out an activity, and the user then performs that activity

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description says a person performs an action themselves, with the help of an online application or software (for example entering data, selecting an option, contacting other people, buying items, or writing a review), and does not say that the process waits for a message, signal, time or condition at that step: Model each such action as one bpmn:userTask placed in the sequence where the description places it, labeled with the action verb and object the description states. Model an optional branch of such actions (for example contacting others only in some cases) as its own userTask in that branch. Do not model the action as a bpmn:sendTask unless sending a message is itself the described unit of work, and do not add a receive element or a second element for the same action.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description says a person performs an action themselves, with the help of an online application or software (for example entering data, selecting an option, contacting other people, buying items, or writing a review), and does not say that the process waits for a message, signal, time or condition at that step

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description says an online tool or system gives the actor instructions or information, and the actor then physically performs the work those instructions describe, with no system involvement in the physical work itself: Model the tool's provision of the instructions as a task that the system performs (a serviceTask, or a userTask if the actor operates the tool), placed before the physical work and labeled with the provision action the description states. Model the actor's hands-on work as a bpmn:manualTask performed by the actor, placed after the instructions and labeled with the physical action the description states. Do not swap these labels, so that the physical work is not labeled as a system task and the receipt of instructions is not labeled as the work itself.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description says an online tool or system gives the actor instructions or information, and the actor then physically performs the work those instructions describe, with no system involvement in the physical work itself
